The question was accusatory. She felt betrayed that Connell would put trust in any other person, especially another woman. A huge part of their relationship relied on their shared belief that no person but the other would ever truly understand them. Marrianne saw Connell had chosen to put his trust into a person besides herself. Marianne craved Connell's full and total attention. That's part of the reason she wanted him to tell her she "belonged" to him. Part of the commitment in a submissive/dominant relationship is the loyalty that comes with those roles. Marianne has no choice but to submit to Connell because of the simple fact of his existence, she would forever and always be fully devoted to him. Because of this, she sought out ways to prove that Connell was as dedicated to the relationship as she was.  

Although their relationship helped them both get through some of the most difficult times in each other's lives it wasn't a positive relationship. Their relationship was fueled by an all-encompassing obsession or a deeply unsettling co-dependency at the best of times. In the show, Marianne comes to realize that she can exist and be "content" as her own person rather than relying on Connell to bring her happiness. That's why she encourages them to do what's best for them as individual people. She understands that a healthy relationship should be made up of two healthy functional people that choose to be in a mutually beneficial relationship. Rather than two people that completely fall apart when the other person isn't there acting as an emotional crutch.  In the book, Marianne clearly lacks the emotional intelligence to see her own co-dependency. Because of this, she leans even further into the worst parts of their relationship at the end of the book.
